verses.kjv: Now the word of the LORD came unto Jonah the son of Amittai, saying,
verses.modern: Now the word of the LORD came to Jonah the son of Amittai, saying,

verses.kjv: Arise, go to Nineveh, that great city, and cry against it; for their wickedness is come up before me.
verses.modern: "Arise, go to Nineveh, that great city, and cry against it; for their wickedness is come up before Me."

verses.kjv: But Jonah rose up to flee unto Tarshish from the presence of the LORD, and went down to Joppa; and he found a ship going to Tarshish: so he paid the fare thereof, and went down into it, to go with them unto Tarshish from the presence of the LORD.
verses.modern: But Jonah rose up to flee to Tarshish, away from the presence of the LORD. He went down to Joppa and found a ship going to Tarshish. So He paid the fare and went down into it, to go with them to Tarshish, away from the presence of the LORD.

verses.kjv: But the LORD sent out a great wind into the sea, and there was a mighty tempest in the sea, so that the ship was like to be broken.
verses.modern: But the LORD sent out a great wind on the sea, and there was a mighty storm at sea, so that the ship was about to be broken apart.

verses.kjv: Then the mariners were afraid, and cried every man unto his god, and cast forth the wares that were in the ship into the sea, to lighten it of them. But Jonah was gone down into the sides of the ship; and he lay, and was fast asleep.
verses.modern: Then the sailors were afraid, and every man cried out to his own god. They threw the cargo of the ship into the sea to lighten it. But Jonah had gone down into the inner part of the ship; and He lay there fast asleep.

verses.kjv: So the shipmaster came to him, and said unto him, What meanest thou, O sleeper? arise, call upon thy God, if so be that God will think upon us, that we perish not.
verses.modern: So the shipmaster came to Him and said, "What do You mean, O sleeper? Arise, call on Your God. Perhaps God will think on us, so that we do not perish."

verses.kjv: And they said every one to his fellow, Come, and let us cast lots, that we may know for whose cause this evil is upon us. So they cast lots, and the lot fell upon Jonah.
verses.modern: And they said to one another, "Come, let us cast lots, so that we may know on whose account this trouble has come on us." So they cast lots, and the lot fell on Jonah.

verses.kjv: Then said they unto him, Tell us, we pray thee, for whose cause this evil is upon us; What is thine occupation? and whence comest thou? what is thy country? and of what people art thou?
verses.modern: Then they said to him, "Please tell us — on whose account has this trouble come on us? What is your occupation? Where do you come from? What is your country? And of what people are you?"

verses.kjv: And he said unto them, I am an Hebrew; and I fear the LORD, the God of heaven, which hath made the sea and the dry land.
verses.modern: And He said to them, "I am a Hebrew, and I fear the LORD, the God of heaven, who made the sea and the dry land."

verses.kjv: Then were the men exceedingly afraid, and said unto him, Why hast thou done this? For the men knew that he fled from the presence of the LORD, because he had told them.
verses.modern: Then the men were greatly afraid and said to Him, "Why have You done this?" For the men knew that He was fleeing from the presence of the LORD, because He had told them.

verses.kjv: Then said they unto him, What shall we do unto thee, that the sea may be calm unto us? for the sea wrought, and was tempestuous.
verses.modern: Then they said to Him, "What shall we do to You, so that the sea may be calm for us?" — for the sea grew more and more stormy.

verses.kjv: And he said unto them, Take me up, and cast me forth into the sea; so shall the sea be calm unto you: for I know that for my sake this great tempest is upon you.
verses.modern: And He said to them, "Take me up and cast me into the sea, and the sea will be calm for You. For I know that this great storm is on You on my account."

verses.kjv: Nevertheless the men rowed hard to bring it to the land; but they could not: for the sea wrought, and was tempestuous against them.
verses.modern: Nevertheless the men rowed hard to bring the ship back to land; but they could not, for the sea grew more and more stormy against them.

verses.kjv: Wherefore they cried unto the LORD, and said, We beseech thee, O LORD, we beseech thee, let us not perish for this man's life, and lay not upon us innocent blood: for thou, O LORD, hast done as it pleased thee.
verses.modern: Therefore they cried out to the LORD and said, "We beg You, O LORD, we beg You, do not let us perish for this man's life. Do not lay innocent blood on us, for You, O LORD, have done as it pleased You."

verses.kjv: So they took up Jonah, and cast him forth into the sea: and the sea ceased from her raging.
verses.modern: So they took Jonah up and cast him into the sea; and the sea ceased from its raging.

verses.kjv: Then the men feared the LORD exceedingly, and offered a sacrifice unto the LORD, and made vows.
verses.modern: Then the men greatly feared the LORD. They offered a sacrifice to the LORD and made vows.

verses.kjv: Now the LORD had prepared a great fish to swallow up Jonah. And Jonah was in the belly of the fish three days and three nights.
verses.modern: Now the LORD had prepared a great fish to swallow up Jonah. And Jonah was in the belly of the fish three days and three nights.

chapters.summary: Jonah fled from the LORD's command to preach to Nineveh and boarded a ship to Tarshish. A great storm struck, the sailors cast lots, and the lot fell on Jonah. At his own word they threw him into the sea, and the storm ceased. The LORD prepared a great fish to swallow Jonah, and he was in its belly three days and three nights.

verses.kjv: Then Jonah prayed unto the LORD his God out of the fish's belly,
verses.modern: Then Jonah prayed to the LORD His God out of the fish's belly,

verses.kjv: And said, I cried by reason of mine affliction unto the LORD, and he heard me; out of the belly of hell cried I, and thou heardest my voice.
verses.modern: and said, "I cried out to the LORD because of my affliction, and He heard me. Out of the belly of hell I cried, and You heard my voice.

verses.kjv: For thou hadst cast me into the deep, in the midst of the seas; and the floods compassed me about: all thy billows and thy waves passed over me.
verses.modern: For You had cast me into the deep, into the midst of the seas; and the floods surrounded me. All Your billows and Your waves passed over me.

verses.kjv: Then I said, I am cast out of thy sight; yet I will look again toward thy holy temple.
verses.modern: Then I said, 'I am cast out of Your sight — yet I will look again toward Your holy temple.'

verses.kjv: The waters compassed me about, even to the soul: the depth closed me round about, the weeds were wrapped about my head.
verses.modern: The waters surrounded me, even to the soul; the deep closed in around me; the weeds were wrapped about my head.

verses.kjv: I went down to the bottoms of the mountains; the earth with her bars was about me for ever: yet hast thou brought up my life from corruption, O LORD my God.
verses.modern: I went down to the bottoms of the mountains; the earth with its bars closed in on me forever. Yet You have brought up my life from corruption, O LORD my God.

verses.kjv: When my soul fainted within me I remembered the LORD: and my prayer came in unto thee, into thine holy temple.
verses.modern: When my soul fainted within me, I remembered the LORD; and my prayer came to You, into Your holy temple.

verses.kjv: They that observe lying vanities forsake their own mercy.
verses.modern: Those who hold to lying vanities forsake their own mercy.

verses.kjv: But I will sacrifice unto thee with the voice of thanksgiving; I will pay that that I have vowed. Salvation is of the LORD.
verses.modern: But I will sacrifice to You with the voice of thanksgiving; I will pay what I have vowed. Salvation is of the LORD."

verses.kjv: And the LORD spake unto the fish, and it vomited out Jonah upon the dry land.
verses.modern: And the LORD spoke to the fish, and it vomited Jonah out on the dry land.

chapters.summary: From inside the belly of the great fish, Jonah prayed to the LORD. He cried out from the depths of the sea, and the LORD heard him. Jonah declared, "Salvation is of the LORD." The LORD spoke to the fish, and it vomited Jonah onto dry land.

verses.kjv: And the word of the LORD came unto Jonah the second time, saying,
verses.modern: And the word of the LORD came to Jonah the second time, saying,

verses.kjv: Arise, go unto Nineveh, that great city, and preach unto it the preaching that I bid thee.
verses.modern: "Arise, go to Nineveh, that great city, and preach to it the preaching that I bid You."

verses.kjv: So Jonah arose, and went unto Nineveh, according to the word of the LORD. Now Nineveh was an exceeding great city of three days' journey.
verses.modern: So Jonah arose and went to Nineveh, according to the word of the LORD. Now Nineveh was an exceedingly great city, three days' journey across.

verses.kjv: And Jonah began to enter into the city a day's journey, and he cried, and said, Yet forty days, and Nineveh shall be overthrown.
verses.modern: And Jonah began to enter into the city a day's journey, and He cried out and said, "Yet forty days, and Nineveh shall be overthrown!"

verses.kjv: So the people of Nineveh believed God, and proclaimed a fast, and put on sackcloth, from the greatest of them even to the least of them.
verses.modern: So the people of Nineveh believed God. They proclaimed a fast, and put on sackcloth, from the greatest of them even to the least of them.

verses.kjv: For word came unto the king of Nineveh, and he arose from his throne, and he laid his robe from him, and covered him with sackcloth, and sat in ashes.
verses.modern: For word came to the king of Nineveh, and he arose from his throne. He laid aside his robe, covered himself with sackcloth, and sat in ashes.

verses.kjv: And he caused it to be proclaimed and published through Nineveh by the decree of the king and his nobles, saying, Let neither man nor beast, herd nor flock, taste any thing: let them not feed, nor drink water:
verses.modern: And he had it proclaimed and published throughout Nineveh, by the decree of the king and his nobles, saying, "Let neither man nor beast, herd nor flock, taste anything. Let them not feed, nor drink water.

verses.kjv: But let man and beast be covered with sackcloth, and cry mightily unto God: yea, let them turn every one from his evil way, and from the violence that is in their hands.
verses.modern: But let man and beast be covered with sackcloth, and cry mightily to God. Let every one turn from his evil way, and from the violence that is in their hands.

verses.kjv: Who can tell if God will turn and repent, and turn away from his fierce anger, that we perish not?
verses.modern: Who can tell if God will turn and repent, and turn away from His fierce anger, so that we do not perish?"

verses.kjv: And God saw their works, that they turned from their evil way; and God repented of the evil, that he had said that he would do unto them; and he did it not.
verses.modern: And God saw their works, that they turned from their evil way; and God repented of the disaster that He had said He would do to them, and He did it not.

chapters.summary: The word of the LORD came to Jonah a second time: "Go to Nineveh." Jonah obeyed and preached, "Yet forty days, and Nineveh shall be overthrown." The entire city believed God — from the king to the least of them — and put on sackcloth and fasted. God saw their repentance and relented from the disaster.

verses.kjv: But it displeased Jonah exceedingly, and he was very angry.
verses.modern: But it displeased Jonah greatly, and he was very angry.

verses.kjv: And he prayed unto the LORD, and said, I pray thee, O LORD, was not this my saying, when I was yet in my country? Therefore I fled before unto Tarshish: for I knew that thou art a gracious God, and merciful, slow to anger, and of great kindness, and repentest thee of the evil.
verses.modern: And He prayed to the LORD and said, "I pray You, O LORD — was this not what I said when I was still in my own country? That is why I fled beforehand to Tarshish. For I knew that You are a gracious God, and merciful, longsuffering, and of great kindness, and One who repents of the evil.

verses.kjv: Therefore now, O LORD, take, I beseech thee, my life from me; for it is better for me to die than to live.
verses.modern: Therefore now, O LORD, I beg You, take my life from me; for it is better for me to die than to live."

verses.kjv: Then said the LORD, Doest thou well to be angry?
verses.modern: Then the LORD said, "Do You do well to be angry?"

verses.kjv: So Jonah went out of the city, and sat on the east side of the city, and there made him a booth, and sat under it in the shadow, till he might see what would become of the city.
verses.modern: So Jonah went out of the city and sat on the east side of the city. There He made Himself a booth and sat under it in the shade, until He might see what would become of the city.

verses.kjv: And the LORD God prepared a gourd, and made it to come up over Jonah, that it might be a shadow over his head, to deliver him from his grief. So Jonah was exceeding glad of the gourd.
verses.modern: And the LORD God prepared a gourd and made it grow up over Jonah, so that it might be a shade over his head, to deliver Him from His discomfort. So Jonah was very glad of the gourd.

verses.kjv: But God prepared a worm when the morning rose the next day, and it smote the root of the gourd that it withered.
verses.modern: But God prepared a worm when the morning rose the next day, and it struck the gourd so that it withered.

verses.kjv: And it came to pass, when the sun did arise, that God prepared a vehement east wind; and the sun beat upon the head of Jonah, that he fainted, and wished in himself to die, and said, It is better for me to die than to live.
verses.modern: And when the sun arose, God prepared a fierce east wind. The sun beat on the head of Jonah, so that he fainted. And he wished within himself to die, and said, "It is better for me to die than to live."

verses.kjv: And God said to Jonah, Doest thou well to be angry for the gourd? And he said, I do well to be angry, even unto death.
verses.modern: And God said to Jonah, "Do you do well to be angry over the gourd?" And He said, "I do well to be angry, even to death."

verses.kjv: Then said the LORD, Thou hast had pity on the gourd, for the which thou hast not laboured, neither madest it grow; which came up in a night, and perished in a night:
verses.modern: Then the LORD said, "You have had pity on the gourd, for which You did not labor, nor make it grow; which came up in a night and perished in a night.

verses.kjv: And should not I spare Nineveh, that great city, wherein are more than sixscore thousand persons that cannot discern between their right hand and their left hand; and also much cattle?
verses.modern: And should I not spare Nineveh, that great city, in which there are more than sixscore thousand persons that cannot discern between their right hand and their left hand — and also much cattle?"

chapters.summary: Jonah was furious that the LORD spared Nineveh and admitted he fled precisely because he knew God was gracious and merciful, longsuffering and abundant in mercy. The LORD prepared a gourd for shade, then a worm to destroy it and a scorching east wind. He rebuked Jonah: "You pity the gourd — should I not pity Nineveh, with more than 120,000 persons who cannot tell their right hand from their left?"
